sentences.text: This is where the well meets the template.
The conductor housing lands in a slot of the template structure, and lower down, the conductor is guided by a ring in the bottom of the structure.
When the riser pulls on the wellhead, the conductor pushes on that ring.
So when has this interface failed, according to the standard?
When the steel reaches zero point two percent plastic strain, the yield strength?
Or at a strain limit, like the five percent, or the two percent, that people attribute to Eurocode three, part one five?

In this follow-up to the acceptance criteria video, we find out which standard owns the interface, what failure means on each side of it, what Eurocode three actually says, and we check the slot ring both ways.
NORSOK U zero zero one names the contacts in Figure J one.
Contact C is between the template structure and the conductor housing, and contact D is at the bottom of the structure.
When the template is in the load path, load path three runs from the wellhead, through the conductor, into the guide structure and down to the seabed.
How much load goes that way is the load share.
It depends on the tolerances and on the relative stiffness of well, template and soil.
The interface has two sides, and each side has its own rule book.
The wellhead side, the conductor housing and the conductor, is checked to Annex B of U zero zero one and the pipe formulas of clause B nine.
That was the first video: the yield strength at zero point two percent plastic strain, and capacities found as loads.
The template side is different.
Clause thirteen point three point six point one says that structural design shall follow I S O thirteen six twenty-eight, part fifteen, clause five point four, and NORSOK N zero zero one.
N zero zero one sends steel design on to N zero zero four, and N zero zero four builds on Eurocode three.
So U zero zero one has no failure criterion of its own for the template steel.
It hands it over.
Before any stress, the interface can fail as a mechanism.
The well grows with temperature, and the template settles.

Clause thirteen point three point six point two asks the template design to account for a relative vertical displacement of one hundred millimetres between template and conductor, unless otherwise specified.
Note d of Table A two makes this a serviceability check, with load factor one point zero: the margins to the upper and lower end stops are checked.
If an end stop is reached, the template is preloaded, and that force goes into separate ultimate limit state load cases.
And the installed template may not lean more than zero point three degrees, unless the tolerance loops allow it.

chapters.title: The template steel: the elastic check

sentences.text: On the template side there are no design factors.
It is load and resistance factor design.

The loads are multiplied by the load factors of N zero zero one, which Table A two lists: one point three on the extreme riser loads in the ultimate limit state, one point zero in the accidental case.
The resistance is divided by a material factor: one point one five for steel in the ultimate limit state, in N zero zero four, and one point zero in the accidental limit state.
And the yield strength?
For a forty millimetre plate of S three fifty-five, the nominal yield strength, f y, is three hundred and forty-five megapascals.
Eurocode three takes it from the product standard: the upper yield strength, or the zero point two percent proof strength when the steel shows no distinct yield point.
So yes, it is the same idea as the zero point two percent offset.
And it is reached at a strain of only zero point one six percent.
The first Eurocode check is elastic.
Clause six point two point one, paragraph five, of part one one: the von Mises stress at the critical point shall not exceed f y divided by gamma M zero.
Here is the lower slot ring, cut from that plate, with the conductor pushing on it between two struts.
At the design contact force of one point six meganewtons, the outer edge behind the contact reaches four hundred and sixteen megapascals.
The limit is three hundred.
Utilisation, one point three nine.
So by the elastic check, the ring has failed.
But that check stops at the first point that yields.
It is the most conservative option, not the only one.
For a plated detail in a finite element model, Eurocode three offers another route: Annex C of part one five, finite element methods of analysis.
It is an informative annex, so the National Annex and your design basis decide whether it is used.
For a stocky part that cannot buckle, like this ring, a materially non-linear analysis is enough.
Where buckling is possible, the geometric non-linearity and the imperfections must be included as well.
Clause C six gives the material models: elastic plastic without strain hardening, with a nominal plateau slope, with linear strain hardening, or a true stress strain curve from tests.
They use characteristic values: f y itself, not divided by the material factor.
Clause C seven puts the factored design loads into the model, multiplied by one load multiplier, alpha, which the analysis increases until a limit state is reached.
And here is the clause you heard about: C eight, the limit state criteria.
Where the structure is susceptible to buckling, the criterion is reaching the maximum load.
In regions in tension, it is reaching a limiting value of the principal membrane strain.
Note one: the National Annex may specify that value, and five percent is recommended.
Note two: other criteria may be used, for example reaching the yield criterion, or limiting the yielded zone.
Membrane means the strain at mid thickness of the shell, not the surface value with plate bending added on top.
Let's run it.
Up to eighty-three percent of the design load, the ring is elastic.
Then the outer edge behind the contact yields, and at one point two five times the design load it has zero point two percent plastic strain.
The plastic zones spread, behind the contact and at the struts.
Without strain hardening, the curve flattens at one point five four: a plastic mechanism.
With linear hardening, it keeps rising.
There is no peak and no buckling, so the five percent strain decides: at one point seven six times the design load.
Clause C nine sets the margin.
The multiplier at the limit state, alpha u, shall be at least alpha one times alpha two.
Alpha one covers the uncertainty of the F E model, calibrated against tests.
Alpha two covers the scatter of loads and resistance: gamma M one where instability governs, gamma M two where fracture governs.
With alpha one equal to one, for a benchmarked model, and alpha two no more than one point three, alpha u of one point seven six passes, and so does one point five three without hardening.
So the ring that failed the elastic check is accepted by the non-linear one, with margin.
Now the two percent.
Annex C contains one strain value, the recommended five percent.
We found no two percent criterion in part one five.
If someone quotes one, ask which document it comes from, and which strain it limits.
And what would it change here?
With hardening, stopping at two percent instead of five lowers the capacity by ten percent.
Without hardening, by only two percent, because the curve is already flat.
There is a catch with every strain limit.
Without hardening, the same load, one point five times the design load, gives one point four percent strain with coarse elements, and two point four percent with fine ones.
The load at the limit hardly moves, but the strain does.
With hardening, the mesh no longer matters.
So a strain limit always comes with a material model, a mesh, and a definition of the strain.
The second generation of Eurocode three develops this into a part of its own, E N nineteen ninety-three, part one fourteen, published in twenty twenty-five.
Check which edition your design basis calls for.
So, when has the template interface failed?
As a mechanism, when the relative displacement uses up the margin to the end stops.
On the wellhead side, when the load exceeds F d times the capacity of Annex B, with the yield strength at zero point two percent plastic strain.
On the template side, by the elastic route, when the von Mises stress at a point reaches f y over gamma M.
And by the non-linear route, at the maximum load or at five percent principal membrane strain, with alpha u at least alpha one times alpha two.
Two percent is not a criterion of Eurocode three, part one five.
The ring, its load and the factors in this video are teaching inputs.
The clauses are on screen, and the notes list what was checked and against which source.
Use the editions and the National Annex of your own design basis.
